newsitem.title: CHINA: IBM China lab sees voice software in a year.
newsitem.headline: IBM China lab sees voice software in a year.

text.p: International Business Machines' Beijing research laboratory is hoping to launch its first voice recognition product for Chinese language users in about one year, company officials said on Tuesday.

The software would be targeted mainly at office workers, who could dictate text into the computer rather than having to learn complex keyboard input methods for Chinese writing, said Donald Tang, the laboratory's assistant director.
Chinese writing consists of thousands of graphically complex characters that require a laborious and memory-taxing method of keyboard entry.

"Speech recognition... is going to be a key priority for IBM because there's a vast audience of potential computer users that are intimidated by the keyboard," said David Yaun, spokesman for the firm's research division.
The importance of the emerging Chinese market meant it was vital for IBM to develop or adapt technologies to fit the unique needs of Chinese users, laboratory director George Wang said.
"This is a very promising emerging market and we see very real potential growth over here," Wang said. "We believe there are lots of technologies... that we need to address in this emerging market."
The laboratory was hoping the programme could hit the market in about one year, assistant director Tang said.
The voice recognition software would have a base dictionary of about 30,000 words, most of which appeared frequently in Chinese newspapers, he said.
The future product could be tailored to specific businesses such as securities, banking, accounting and law, he added.
The programme was based on Mandarin Chinese but would be able to recognise different accents in order to cope with the huge array of local dialects in China, he said.
Industry analysts have estimated China's sales of personal computers to be between two and three million units in 1996, and predict sales could reach 10 million units by the year 2000.
